summary: Karpathy proposes compiling raw sources once into a persistent interlinked Markdown wiki that agents query instead of re-running RAG each time, enabling knowledge that compounds across ingestion runs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already ships skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). The compounding-wiki pattern maps to the known gap of executor prompts not receiving distilled skills, which is tracked by HID-188. No new capability gap.

summary: Karpathy introduced 'agentic engineering' as a discipline: spec design + diff review + eval loops, with humans maintaining conceptual ownership and models handling iteration. 9-rule framework for autonomous dev workflows.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already implements the core loop (plan → review → implement → review). No concrete implementable gap identified beyond what already exists in the state machine.

source: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents (arXiv 2604.10674)
summary: Turns agent's own trajectories into dynamic training-only supervision by summarizing them into compact natural language skills (teacher-conditioned), which the student internalizes via distillation — no human labels needed.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — This is a model training / fine-tuning approach. AgentForge orchestrates off-the-shelf CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex) without training them. Not feasible to implement.

summary: Frames skill utilization as a credit-assignment problem during on-policy RL training — agents learn which skills to retrieve, when to trust, correct, and internalize them.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL training approach, out of scope for an orchestrator that wraps existing CLI models. No actionable gap in AgentForge's architecture.

source: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic RL (arXiv 2606.26790)
summary: Extracts hierarchical skill supervision from completed on-policy trajectories and distills it back into the policy model via RL.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL fine-tuning approach requiring model training. Not applicable to AgentForge's subprocess-orchestration model.

source: Seed: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic RL (arXiv 2607.14777)
summary: Converts completed on-policy trajectories into hindsight skills and distills back into the policy model iteratively.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Same RL training paradigm as OPID and UCOB. Out of scope.

summary: LangMem adds semantic, episodic, and procedural memory tiers to LangGraph agents via checkpointer-based short/long-term patterns; legacy memory classes deprecated in 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Episodic memory for AgentForge is already tracked by HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory injection into planner and executor). No new gap identified.

source: Self-Improving AI Coding Agents Through Accumulated Behavioral Rules (arXiv 2607.13091)
summary: Closed-loop framework where coding agents accumulate distilled behavioral rules from execution traces — successful patterns become reusable rules injected into future runs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Directly maps to AgentForge's distillationAgent.ts + agentSkillRepository.ts which already does this. The remaining gap (executor not receiving skills) is tracked by HID-188. No new issue needed.

source: Arize: Closing the Loop — Coding Agents, Telemetry, and Self-Improving Software (blog)
summary: Argues that telemetry-grounded reflection loops (objective checks like running code, PRMs) are the strongest 2026 reliability lever for coding agents, with memory-based learning as the most practical near-term form.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Token/cost telemetry is tracked by HID-163. Reflection / partial retry tracked by HID-186 and HID-93. All covered.

source: DeerFlow v2.0 — ByteDance long-horizon SuperAgent harness (GitHub trending Feb 2026)
summary: ByteDance open-source multi-agent research harness that hit #1 GitHub trending in February 2026, focused on long-horizon tasks with multi-agent decomposition.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Multi-agent decomposition architecture fundamentally different from AgentForge's sequential state machine. Deliberately out of scope; parallel/multi-agent execution was rejected as a design choice.

source: Princeton NLP: Single agent matches multi-agent on 64% of tasks (2026 research finding)
summary: Princeton NLP research found that a single agent matched or outperformed multi-agent systems on 64% of benchmarked tasks when given the same tools and context.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Validates AgentForge's current sequential single-agent-per-stage design choice. No new capability needed; this is confirmatory evidence for the existing architecture.
